facts.fact_text: On 26 September 2005, Hyde Park (the first applicant) applied to the Chişinău Municipal Council for authorisation to hold a peaceful rally in the Stefan cel Mare Park in Chişinău.
The peaceful rally for which Hyde Park sought authorisation was planned for 14 October 2005.
The peaceful rally for which Hyde Park sought authorisation was in support of freedom of speech.
On 7 October 2005, the Chişinău Municipal Council rejected Hyde Park's application to hold a rally in the Stefan cel Mare Park on 14 October 2005.
On 2 December 2005, the Chişinău Court of Appeal dismissed the applicants' action challenging the Chişinău Municipal Council's refusal to authorise the rally.
On 3 May 2006, the Supreme Court of Justice dismissed Hyde Park's (the first applicant's) appeal on points of law against the Chişinău Court of Appeal's judgment.

Section 6(1) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that assemblies shall be conducted peacefully, without any sort of weapons, and shall ensure the protection of participants and the environment, without impeding the normal use of public highways, road traffic and the operation of economic undertakings and without degenerating into acts of violence capable of endangering the public order and the physical integrity and life of persons or their property.

Section 7 of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that assemblies shall be suspended in the following circumstances: denial and defamation of the State and of the people; incitement to war or aggression and incitement to hatred on ethnic, racial or religious grounds; incitement to discrimination, territorial separatism or public violence; acts that undermine the constitutional order.

Section 8(1) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that assemblies may be conducted in squares, streets, parks and other public places in cities, towns and villages, and also in public buildings.

Section 8(2) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that it shall be forbidden to conduct an assembly in the buildings of the public authorities, the local authorities, prosecutors' offices, the courts or companies with armed security.

Section 8(3)(a) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that it shall be forbidden to conduct assemblies within fifty metres of the parliament building, the residence of the president of Moldova, the seat of the government, the Constitutional Court and the Supreme Court of Justice.

Section 8(3)(b) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that it shall be forbidden to conduct assemblies within twenty-five metres of the buildings of the central administrative authority, the local public authorities, courts, prosecutors' offices, police stations, prisons and social rehabilitation institutions, military installations, railway stations, airports, hospitals, companies which use dangerous equipment and machines, and diplomatic institutions.

Section 11(1) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that not later than fifteen days prior to the date of the assembly, the organiser shall submit a notification to the Municipal Council, a specimen of which is set out in the annex which forms an integral part of the Act.

Section 12(1) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that the prior notification shall be examined by the local government of the town or village at the latest five days before the date of the assembly.

Section 12(6) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that the local authorities can reject an application to hold an assembly only if, after having consulted the police, they have obtained convincing evidence that the provisions of Sections 6 and 7 of the Assemblies Act will be breached with serious consequences for society.

Section 14(1) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that a decision rejecting the application for holding an assembly shall be reasoned and presented in writing, and shall contain reasons for refusing to issue the authorisation.
The Chişinău Municipal Council rejected Hyde Park's application on the ground that on 14 October 2005 a number of events were planned in the city centre, including in the Stefan cel Mare Park.

The Chişinău Court of Appeal considered that since other events were scheduled to take place in the Stefan cel Mare Park on 14 October 2005, such as exhibitions, sports events, concerts and other demonstrations, Hyde Park's rally might hinder those events.
The Chişinău Court of Appeal considered that Hyde Park's rally might endanger public order.

The Supreme Court of Justice reiterated that authorising Hyde Park's rally at the same time as other cultural and sports demonstrations in the Stefan cel Mare Park ran the risk of resulting in violent clashes and thus endangered public order.
